clean.pr_title: refactor(tokenizer): generalize backslash escape handling, report unterminated escapes
clean.pr_body:
Prepares the tokenizer for decoding backslash escapes in more dialects. Numeric escapes are now checked before the fixed escape sequences, which some dialects need (e.g. `\000` vs `\0`), and control characters are generated with the dialect's numeric escape in the base generator instead of only in Snowflake. No dialect's output changes.

It also fixes a crash: an escape at the end of an unterminated string, e.g. `'\n`, raised an `IndexError` instead of reporting the missing quote.

clean.head: f3b7c6cb737c3d6c798f0c6b408ec8c9ffea6f4b
clean.sha_method: squash merge commit and its first parent
clean.pr_body:
Found another goofy thing we've been working around in Superset, trying to fix upstream where it belongs.

Dremio's `REGEXP_SPLIT(string, pattern, mode, limit)` takes a required `mode` argument (e.g. `'ALL'`) positioned ahead of `limit`, which is a shape the shared `exp.RegexpSplit` didn't have a slot for.

This adds `mode` to `RegexpSplit.arg_types`, appended *after* `limit` so existing 2/3-arg positional callers via `from_arg_list` (Doris `SPLIT_BY_STRING`, ClickHouse `SPLITBYREGEXP`, DuckDB `STR_SPLIT_REGEX`/`STRING_SPLIT_REGEX`, Hive `SPLIT`) keep mapping their existing args unchanged. 

Dremio's own parser/generator build and render the args in the dialect's real order (`this`, `expression`, `mode`, `limit`) via an explicit builder rather than relying on the shared positional `from_arg_list`.

Found this while rebasing Superset's local Dremio dialect (which previously shadowed sqlglot's native one, see [apache/superset#43099](https://github.com/apache/superset/pull/43099)) onto sqlglot's `DremioParser`/`DremioGenerator`. Superset had a local-only `REGEXP_SPLIT` override to fill this gap.

Tests:
- `tests/dialects/test_dremio.py::test_regexp_split` (new)
- Full `tests/dialects/test_dremio.py` suite: 23 passed
- Cross-checked other `RegexpSplit` consumers for regressions: `test_doris.py`, `test_clickhouse.py`, `test_duckdb.py`, `test_hive.py` — 104 passed
- Full test suite: 1213 passed, 2 skipped

clean.pr_title: refactor(shared, json-schema): reuse getOwn for own-property lookups
clean.pr_body:
`get()` in `@orpc/shared` and the property lookup in `JsonSchemaCoercer` were hand-rolled copies of `getOwn`; they now call it. The coercer's `properties !== undefined` ternary is gone in favor of the same `?? {}` default its `patternProperties` lookup already uses.

## Testing

- New RPC and OpenAPI serializer tests pin that a blob or special value stored under an own `__proto__` key, or behind an own `constructor` → `prototype` chain, is restored in place with the global `Object.prototype` untouched and the container never re-parented.
- `pnpm vitest run` across client, openapi, json-schema and shared, `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm type:check` pass.

## Not changed

- The RPC and OpenAPI deserializer walks and `getRouter` / `getRouterContract` keep their existing reads and writes. The deserializers already verify every segment with `Object.hasOwn` before reading it, and router paths come from the router definition rather than the request, so switching them to `getOwn` / `setOwn` would only add a check per segment.

clean.head: fc60e4b837ffc6d947d36175eda4ba6eb5396218
clean.sha_method: squash merge commit and its first parent
clean.pr_body:
`Infinity` and `-Infinity` now round-trip through the RPC serializer. Before, they became `null` with no meta, so `client.setLimit({ max: Infinity })` reached the server as `{ max: null }`. A new built-in `infinity` handler sends them as `"Infinity"` / `"-Infinity"` and rejects any other value on deserialize, like the other built-ins.

The OpenAPI serializer gets a matching `infinity` handler that outputs `null`, like `nan`, so both serializers share the same built-in keys. ±Infinity is now left out of form data and query strings too; before, a GET sent `max=Infinity` and the server received the string `"Infinity"`, while a JSON body sent `null`.

This is the ±Infinity half of #2152 on its own, without the custom-handler change that CodSpeed flags there. If this merges first, #2152 can drop its `infinity` part.

## Things to review

- **RPC wire compatibility:** `infinity` is a new meta type. A peer on an older version rejects it with `type "infinity" is not supported` instead of silently reading `null`. Payloads without ±Infinity are unaffected. The same applies to `@orpc/publisher` events stored with this serializer.
- **OpenAPI output stays spec-valid:** ±Infinity is `null`, not a string, because JSON has no Infinity and the generated spec says `type: number`.
- **Naming:** the meta key is lowercase like every other key (`nan`, `bigint`, `url`). The RPC json value uses JavaScript's own spelling (`String(Infinity)`), which Python's `json`, JSON5 and superjson also use.

## Performance

- Both inlined number paths check `Number.isFinite` first, so finite numbers still take one check. A same-run bench of the RPC serializer, old vs new, came out even: 1.00x on the 100KB payload, 1.08x in favor of new on a number-heavy one.

## Testing

- RPC: ±Infinity is added to the shared built-in type fixtures (root and `packages/bun`), so it round-trips through the serializer unit tests, `RPCSerializer` tests and every e2e transport. The wire-format, generic-path and mistyped-payload tests cover it too. Against the previous serializer, 41 of these tests fail.
- OpenAPI: tests cover ±Infinity becoming `null`, the generic path, and ±Infinity being left out of form data. All 3 fail against the previous serializer.
- `pnpm vitest run packages/client/src/rpc-json-serializer.test.ts packages/client/src/rpc-serializer.test.ts tests/rpc` (558 tests), `pnpm vitest run packages/openapi tests/openapi` (499 tests), `bun test tests/rpc/data-transfer.test.ts` in `packages/bun`, eslint and the `@orpc/client` / `@orpc/openapi` type-checks pass.

## Docs

- The RPC and OpenAPI serializer docs tables and the `handlers` JSDoc list the `infinity` key.

clean.head: 75217411695b9e36dafc5d502401fb74d280058b
clean.sha_method: squash merge commit and its first parent
clean.pr_title: perf: iterate own keys with Object.keys instead of Object.entries
clean.pr_body:
Own-key loops on hot paths now use `Object.keys` with an indexed read instead of `Object.entries`, so the serializers, bracket notation, the JSON schema coercer, `clone` and the batch header loops no longer allocate a `[key, value]` pair per property. Two loops that still visited inherited keys are fixed as well.

## Fixes

- `isProcedureUtilsOptions` (tanstack-query, pinia-colada) no longer reads inherited keys; its `=== undefined` check satisfied `guard-for-in` without filtering the prototype chain.
- `buildErrorResponse` drops its `as ErrorMap` cast, since `Object.keys` over the `any`-typed error map needs none.

## Performance

Repo benches, three rounds per variant in a rotated order, median gain vs `main`:

| Bench | `Object.keys` | `for...in` + `Object.hasOwn` |
|---|---|---|
| RPC serializer 1KB / 100KB / 5MB | +11% / +8% / +11% | +13% / +22% / +18% |
| OpenAPI serializer 1KB / 100KB / 5MB | +30% / +29% / +34% | +21% / +19% / +38% |
| 5MB with files, both serializers | +6% to +8% | +7% to +10% |
| JSON schema coercer, 7 cases | +10% to +34% | +6% to +31% |

Every case was faster than `main` in every round for both variants. The difference between the two variants is within the run-to-run spread of `main` (2% to 21% depending on the case).

Microbench on JSON-shaped objects (Node 24, ns per key): `Object.keys` and the guarded `for...in` tie on fast-mode objects at about 19 to 25. On dictionary-mode objects `Object.keys` wins, 43 vs 68 at 20 keys with a null prototype and 67 vs 94 at 500 keys, while `Object.entries` costs 210 to 230. `Object.keys` also needs no guard, so it is used everywhere.

## Notes

- Loops whose indexed read would need a type cast or a non-null assertion keep `Object.entries`: the server router walkers and implementer, the Nest contract and params loops, the MSW utils, `serializeHeaders`, `resolveBasePathMeta`, `minifyRouterContract` and the tRPC lazy loop. All run at setup time except `serializeHeaders` and the Nest params loop.

## Testing

- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm -w type:check` and vitest for the touched packages plus `tests/` pass.
